name: Upper Trishuli-1
sentences: The project consists of a 100.9-m-wide and 29.5-m high diversion dam in a narrow gorge located in the Trishuli River 275 m downstream of the confluence of the Langtang Khola (tributary) with the Bhote Khosi River, about 70 km to the north-east of Kathmandu.

The diversion dam will create a small 2.1 ha impoundment and divert, via two intake tunnels each with a gate size of 3.35 x 6.50 meters and a total length of approximately 285 meters, up to 76 m3/s of water through a powerhouse with a 216 MW capacity, returning the water to the Trishuli River approximately 10.7 km downstream of the dam.

The project is designed to operate continuously as a run-of-river facility and will connect to a new Chilime–Trishuli transmission line via a 1.1-km long, high voltage extension from the UT-1 take-off yard.

The project is located in an area with generally good air quality, but is located adjacent to a national park, so any increase in pollution levels will be minimized to the extent feasible in accordance with the WBG Environmental, Health, and Safety Guidelines as defined in the proposed management of fugitive dust and vehicular/power emissions which are under the responsibility of the EPC contractor, and which are both covered in the Air Quality Management Plan, of the CESMMP.

As described earlier, the project involves construction of 11.8 km of access roads from Mailung Khola up to the project dam, half of which has already been completed and repaired post-earthquake.

sentences: The new NEPCO transmission line to which the project will interconnect is expected to be around 18 km long and will link a 132 kV substation in the town of Tafila with a substation at Jordan Wind Power Company’s (JWPC’s) 117 MW Tafila wind farm located south of the project site.

The project site is located within Bseira District in Tafila Governorate.

The closest communities include (i) Um Sarab and Bseira which are located at distances of 1 and 3 km from the western site boundary, respectively; (ii) Gharandal, located 1.3 km to the south, and (iii) Ain Baida, located 4 km north west of the site.
The site is at an altitude of roughly 1400 m, about 10 km from the eastern margin of the Rift Valley in Jordan’s Sharah Mountains – also known as the Southern Uplands - roughly 130 km south of Amman.

Dana Biosphere Reserve is located around 7.5 km to the south west of the site and the closest boundary of the Dana Important Bird Area (IBA), which encompasses the Reserve, is located around 3 km away.

The site is around 3.5 km north east of Jordan Wind Power Company’s (JWPC’s) operating 117 MW Tafila wind farm (IFC project 31627, the Environmental & Social (E&S) review summary of which can be viewed here: https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/ESRS/31627 ) and around 3 km south west of the planned 49.5 MW Abour wind farm to be developed by Xenel (IFC project 35348, the E&S review summary of which can be viewed here: https://disclosures.ifc.org/#/projectDetail/ESRS/35348 ).

There are no permanent dwellings or other structures within a kilometer of any turbine location, although several temporary agricultural shelters are dotted around the site and wheat is grown seasonally on certain parcels.
The nearest receptors include homes in Um Sarab settlement which are located around 1 km to the west of the nearest turbines.

Biodiversity-related risks are significant: as described in the project description, this project forms part of a cluster of existing and planned wind power projects located east of Dana Biosphere Reserve, a nationally legally protected and a UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Reserve (MAB).

The Dana Biosphere Reserve is located within a Key Biodiversity Area (KBA) as recognized by the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN), and an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area (IBA) as recognized by BirdLife International due to the diverse assemblage of breeding birds of unusually mixed bio-geographical conditions present in the area.
Both the Reserve and IBA/KBA are located to the west of the project site, in the Rift Valley/Red Sea flyway for migratory birds, the second most frequented flyway worldwide.

Noise modelling shows that operational turbine noise levels will remain within Jordanian and World Bank Group noise thresholds at the nearest sensitive receptors located around 1 km west of the nearest turbines.

This turbine site adjustment process also fulfils Jordanian permitting requirements for the site which require a buffer of 1 km to be maintained between wind turbines and the nearest residential receptor(s).

Shadow flicker effects modeled during the ESIA indicated that several exceedances of the WBG Guidelines threshold limits of 30 mins / day or 30 days / year (worst case) could be expected in the morning hours at certain homes located to the west of the wind farm.
The turbines will be barely visible from the Dana Nature Reserve, the most sensitive area with respect to tourism, located around 7.5 km from site and mostly shielded by topography.

Water requirements will be low during windfarm construction (5 m3/day) and operation (0.5 m3/day); the project will obtain water from the town water supply in Tafila, which is located around 6 km from the site.
Jordan is located along one of the most important migration flyways in the world, namely the Rift Valley / Red Sea Flyway.
The eastern edge of the Great Rift Valley lies approximately 6 km to the west of the project site.

As noted in the project description, the project site is located around 7.5 km northeast of the Dana Biosphere Reserve, an important stopover point for migratory birds, and around 3 km northeast of the outer eastern edge of the Dana IBA, which engulfs the Reserve and which is also an important bird breeding area.
Given its location however near the Rift Valley margins, it is still potentially sensitive, particularly with respect to birds.

Evidence from baseline vantage point bird surveys indicate that the project site is not located within a migration bottleneck and birds typically migrate along a ‘broad-front’ as they pass over the site.
Monitoring will be conducted for an initial 3-year period from two strategically located vantage points that collectively allow bird observers to view the whole project site for bird flight activity.
During the migration periods a single bird observer will be located at each of two vantage points and daily monitoring will be targeted to cover peak migration activity periods.
A similar approach to mitigating bird and bat-related risks has been adopted for IFC’s investment at Tafila WPP, 3.5 km from the project site.

sentences: The project is situated approximately 5 km southwest of Aysha town and is accessed from the Dire Dawa–Aysha–Dewele–Djibouti transport corridor.

The wider project lease area covers approximately 84.46 km² of predominantly arid to semi-arid pastoral land under customary land tenure used by Issa-Somali pastoralist communities for seasonal grazing and migration.

Emergency Preparedness and Response: Due to the project’s remote location and limited availability of public emergency services, effective emergency preparedness and response arrangements for the project will be critical.

For the project, OHS risks are expected to be significant due to the scale of construction activities, remote location, heavy lifting, working at heights, traffic and transportation movements, and the establishment of worker accommodation facilities.
Workers’ Accommodation: Given the remote location of the project, establishing workers’ accommodation camp at the project site is considered necessary.

Given the project is located in an arid to semi-arid pastoral context, as per the ESAP#12, the project will undertake a water supply source assessment to identify sustainable water sourcing solutions that avoid adverse impacts on community water access in consultation with the community, relevant authorities and the EPC contractor.

While the ESIA commits to managing waste in accordance with the waste hierarchy, given the remote location, suitable licensed waste management and disposal facilities are not available in the project region.
Considering the project location, off-site wastewater treatment facilities are not available and thus the project will need to be self-sufficient in this regard.

PS4: Community Health, Safety and Security Community Health and Safety: The project may pose community H&S risks during construction and operation due to its scale, remote location, interaction with pastoralist communities, worker influx, and use of heavy equipment and materials.

Shadow flicker impacts: Based on the ESIA and shadow flicker (SF) impact assessment, no shadow flicker impacts are expected for the sensitive receptors at the nearest settlements - Aysha, (4.2 km north east from the closest WTG), and Lasarat (approximately 2.8 km south west from its closest WTG).
A conservative 2 km buffer was generated around the WTGs as part of the SF impact assessment which clearly illustrates that sensitive receptors are outside this zone.

However, certain “possible settlement sites” used by nomadic herders have been identified in the northern portion of the project area which fall within zones where SF exposure is predicted to exceed guideline values, including areas located beyond the established operational safety setback.

Lastly, the SF impacts are estimated to exceed at two ritual sites i.e. (i) Ritual Site 01 - located in the village of Kelewle (at about 1 km from the nearest WTG): It is used three times a year to hold religious festivals like Eid-al-Fitir, Eid-al-Adha and Mowlid.

This site is expected to experience more than 30 minutes of shadow flicker effects per day at various times throughout the year with the highest incidence being in November. (ii) Ritual Site 03 - located in the village of Aligire (at about 450 m from the nearest WTG): It is used by the sub-clan Sheika for gatherings which take place once a year (usually initiated when demand arises due to a crisis such as conflict, drought, epidemics or the death of influential personalities).

During this time, people from different areas, including Degego, Lasarat, Aysha, Dire Dawa and Djibuti travel to the site for this occasion and spend 2-3 days on this location, where they slaughter goats and cattle to pray for peace and prosperity.
The project is also located in Zone 4, which is classified as a region of the highest seismic hazard.

PS 5: Land Acquisition and Involuntary Resettlement The project has secured a lease over approximately 84.46 km² of land from the Somali Regional State Environmental Protection and Rural Land Administration Bureau for the period 2025–2049.
PS6: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources The project is located within the Djibouti xeric shrublands ecoregion.
The nearest Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) are the Ali Sabieh – Assamo 50 km northeast and Salak 60 km east of the project site in Djibouti and Somalia respectively.

PS7: Indigenous Peoples Identification and Screening of Indigenous Peoples: The project is located entirely within Aysha Woreda, Somali Regional State, an area inhabited exclusively by members of the Issa Clan and its sub-clans.

Land Acquisition for the project and related PS 7 requirements: The project secured a land lease of approximately 84.46 km² from the Somali Regional State in 2024, for a period extending from October 2024 to June 2049.

However, the project will impose temporary construction-phase access restrictions across approximately 6.49 km² (8% of the lease area) and permanent operational-phase safety buffers across approximately 15.21 km² (18% of the lease area) around each WTG, restricting settlement while permitting grazing and movement.
Less than 1% of the lease area (approximately 0.751 km²) will be permanently occupied by project infrastructure.
The SLIP identifies approximately 43 burial grounds, and three ritual sites located within the project lease area.

The nearest community settlement is the Ras Ghareb city, 9 km to the southeast.The Project site avoids impacts on physical or economic displacement or from shadow flicker or operational noise-related nuisance, due to its distance from any settlements.

Further, as concluded from the Project ESIA, impact related to air and noise emissions, visual intrusion, and to potential shadow flicker are of minor significance due to the lack of nearby sensitive receptors and distance (9 km) from the nearest community receptors, Ras Ghareb city.

As informed by the ESDD process, the closest suitable solid waste, wastewater, and hazardous waste treatment and disposal facilities are located in Hurghada city, Rash Ghareb city, and Alexandria or Helwan city respectively.

AWPC will monitor the implementation of this management plan by the EPC & O&M contractors via regular audits. (ESAP #4b) PS 6: Biodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Management of Living Natural Resources The project is situated in the Red Sea Coastal Desert ecoregion.
